# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching fresh subagent per task, with two-stage review after each: spec compliance review first, then code quality review.

**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review (spec then quality) = high quality, fast iteration

## When to Use

```dot
digraph when_to_use {
    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];
    "subagent-driven-development" [shape=box];
    "executing-plans" [shape=box];
    "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];

    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Tasks mostly independent?" [label="yes"];
    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Stay in this session?" [label="yes"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no - tightly coupled"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="yes"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Two-stage review after each task: spec compliance first, then code quality
- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)

## The Process

```dot
digraph process {
    rankdir=TB;

    subgraph cluster_per_task {
        label="Per Task";
        "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Implementer subagent asks questions?" [shape=diamond];
        "Answer questions, provide context" [shape=box];
        "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" [shape=box];
        "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" [shape=diamond];
        "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" [shape=box];
        "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" [shape=diamond];
        "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" [shape=box];
        "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" [shape=box];
    }

    "Read plan, extract all tasks with full text, note context, create TodoWrite" [shape=box];
    "More tasks remain?" [shape=diamond];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" [shape=box];
    "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch" [shape=box style=filled fillcolor=lightgreen];

    "Read plan, extract all tasks with full text, note context, create TodoWrite" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)";
    "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" -> "Implementer subagent asks questions?";
    "Implementer subagent asks questions?" -> "Answer questions, provide context" [label="yes"];
    "Answer questions, provide context" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)";
    "Implementer subagent asks questions?" -> "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" -> "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)";
    "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?";
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" -> "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="re-review"];
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="yes"];
    "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?";
    "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" -> "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" -> "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="re-review"];
    "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" -> "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" [label="yes"];
    "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" -> "More tasks remain?";
    "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [label="yes"];
    "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" [label="no"];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" -> "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch";
}
```

## Model Selection

Use the least powerful model that can handle each role to conserve cost and increase speed.

**Mechanical implementation tasks** (isolated functions, clear specs, 1-2 files): use a fast, cheap model. Most implementation tasks are mechanical when the plan is well-specified.

**Integration and judgment tasks** (multi-file coordination, pattern matching, debugging): use a standard model.

**Architecture, design, and review tasks**: use the most capable available model.

**Task complexity signals:**
- Touches 1-2 files with a complete spec → cheap model
- Touches multiple files with integration concerns → standard model
- Requires design judgment or broad codebase understanding → most capable model

## Handling Implementer Status

Implementer subagents report one of four statuses. Handle each appropriately:

**DONE:** Proceed to spec compliance review.

**DONE_WITH_CONCERNS:** The implementer completed the work but flagged doubts. Read the concerns before proceeding. If the concerns are about correctness or scope, address them before review. If they're observations (e.g., "this file is getting large"), note them and proceed to review.

**NEEDS_CONTEXT:** The implementer needs information that wasn't provided. Provide the missing context and re-dispatch.

**BLOCKED:** The implementer cannot complete the task. Assess the blocker:
1. If it's a context problem, provide more context and re-dispatch with the same model
2. If the task requires more reasoning, re-dispatch with a more capable model
3. If the task is too large, break it into smaller pieces
4. If the plan itself is wrong, escalate to the human

**Never** ignore an escalation or force the same model to retry without changes. If the implementer said it's stuck, something needs to change.

## Prompt Templates

- `./implementer-prompt.md` - Dispatch implementer subagent
- `./spec-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch spec compliance reviewer subagent
- `./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent

## Example Workflow

```
You: I'm using Subagent-Driven Development to execute this plan.

[Read plan file once: docs/superpowers/plans/feature-plan.md]
[Extract all 5 tasks with full text and context]
[Create TodoWrite with all tasks]

Task 1: Hook installation script

[Get Task 1 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: "Before I begin - should the hook be installed at user or system level?"

You: "User level (~/.config/superpowers/hooks/)"

Implementer: "Got it. Implementing now..."
[Later] Implementer:
  - Implemented install-hook command
  - Added tests, 5/5 passing
  - Self-review: Found I missed --force flag, added it
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant - all requirements met, nothing extra

[Get git SHAs, dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Good test coverage, clean. Issues: None. Approved.

[Mark Task 1 complete]

Task 2: Recovery modes

[Get Task 2 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: [No questions, proceeds]
Implementer:
  - Added verify/repair modes
  - 8/8 tests passing
  - Self-review: All good
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ❌ Issues:
  - Missing: Progress reporting (spec says "report every 100 items")
  - Extra: Added --json flag (not requested)

[Implementer fixes issues]
Implementer: Removed --json flag, added progress reporting

[Spec reviewer reviews again]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant now

[Dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Solid. Issues (Important): Magic number (100)

[Implementer fixes]
Implementer: Extracted PROGRESS_INTERVAL constant

[Code reviewer reviews again]
Code reviewer: ✅ Approved

[Mark Task 2 complete]

...

[After all tasks]
[Dispatch final code-reviewer]
Final reviewer: All requirements met, ready to merge

Done!
```

## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - REQUIRED: Set up isolated workspace before starting
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:requesting-code-review** - Code review template for reviewer subagents
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

**Subagents should use:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - Subagents follow TDD for each task

**Alternative workflow:**
- **superpowers:executing-plans** - Use for parallel session instead of same-session execution

# Implementer Subagent Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching an implementer subagent.

```
Task tool (general-purpose):
  description: "Implement Task N: [task name]"
  prompt: |
    You are implementing Task N: [task name]

    ## Task Description

    [FULL TEXT of task from plan - paste it here, don't make subagent read file]

    ## Context

    [Scene-setting: where this fits, dependencies, architectural context]

    ## Before You Begin

    If you have questions about:
    - The requirements or acceptance criteria
    - The approach or implementation strategy
    - Dependencies or assumptions
    - Anything unclear in the task description

    **Ask them now.** Raise any concerns before starting work.

    ## Your Job

    Once you're clear on requirements:
    1. Implement exactly what the task specifies
    2. Write tests (following TDD if task says to)
    3. Verify implementation works
    4. Commit your work
    5. Self-review (see below)
    6. Report back

    Work from: [directory]

    **While you work:** If you encounter something unexpected or unclear, **ask questions**.
    It's always OK to pause and clarify. Don't guess or make assumptions.

    ## Code Organization

    You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more
    reliable when files are focused. Keep this in mind:
    - Follow the file structure defined in the plan
    - Each file should have one clear responsibility with a well-defined interface
    - If a file you're creating is growing beyond the plan's intent, stop and report
      it as DONE_WITH_CONCERNS — don't split files on your own without plan guidance
    - If an existing file you're modifying is already large or tangled, work carefully
      and note it as a concern in your report
    - In existing codebases, follow established patterns. Improve code you're touching
      the way a good developer would, but don't restructure things outside your task.

    ## When You're in Over Your Head

    It is always OK to stop and say "this is too hard for me." Bad work is worse than
    no work. You will not be penalized for escalating.

    **STOP and escalate when:**
    - The task requires architectural decisions with multiple valid approaches
    - You need to understand code beyond what was provided and can't find clarity
    - You feel uncertain about whether your approach is correct
    - The task involves restructuring existing code in ways the plan didn't anticipate
    - You've been reading file after file trying to understand the system without progress

    **How to escalate:** Report back with status BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT. Describe
    specifically what you're stuck on, what you've tried, and what kind of help you need.
    The controller can provide more context, re-dispatch with a more capable model,
    or break the task into smaller pieces.

    ## Before Reporting Back: Self-Review

    Review your work with fresh eyes. Ask yourself:

    **Completeness:**
    - Did I fully implement everything in the spec?
    - Did I miss any requirements?
    - Are there edge cases I didn't handle?

    **Quality:**
    - Is this my best work?
    - Are names clear and accurate (match what things do, not how they work)?
    - Is the code clean and maintainable?

    **Discipline:**
    - Did I avoid overbuilding (YAGNI)?
    - Did I only build what was requested?
    - Did I follow existing patterns in the codebase?

    **Testing:**
    - Do tests actually verify behavior (not just mock behavior)?
    - Did I follow TDD if required?
    - Are tests comprehensive?

    If you find issues during self-review, fix them now before reporting.

    ## Report Format

    When done, report:
    - **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT
    - What you implemented (or what you attempted, if blocked)
    - What you tested and test results
    - Files changed
    - Self-review findings (if any)
    - Any issues or concerns

    Use DONE_WITH_CONCERNS if you completed the work but have doubts about correctness.
    Use BLOCKED if you cannot complete the task. Use NEEDS_CONTEXT if you need
    information that wasn't provided. Never silently produce work you're unsure about.
```

Replace the existing `GetMetadataBranchTree` function in `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go` (currently around line 763) with:

```go
// GetMetadataRefTree returns the tree object at the given committed-metadata
// ref. Callers pass the ref name explicitly:
//
//   - For v1-pinned reads (fetch chain, blob prefetch):
//     plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
//   - For topology-aware reads (everything else):
//     checkpoint.ResolveCommittedRefs(ctx).Read
func GetMetadataRefTree(repo *git.Repository, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) (*object.Tree, error) {
	r, err := repo.Reference(ref, true)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read ref %s: %w", ref, err)
	}
	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(r.Hash())
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read commit at %s: %w", ref, err)
	}
	tree, err := commit.Tree()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read tree at %s: %w", ref, err)
	}
	return tree, nil
}
```

### Task 3: Migrate the rewind picker to the topology read ref

**Files:**
- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go` (~line 164: change ref argument)
- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_test.go` (add new test next to `TestShadowStrategy_GetRewindPoints_NoShadowBranch`)

TDD red-to-green. The test is written first, fails because the picker still reads v1, then passes after the picker's ref argument is changed.

The test setup writes the checkpoint metadata to v1, then captures v1's tip, re-points v1 backward to the initial commit, and points the v1.1 mirror at the captured tip. The result: only the mirror's tree carries the checkpoint, and v1 has nothing useful at the metadata path. `listCheckpoints` (topology-aware) finds the checkpoint via the mirror, the commit log walk finds the trailer at HEAD, but the metadata tree read on the v1 ref hits a tree without the checkpoint subdirectory — yielding an empty `SessionPrompt`. After the fix, the metadata read uses the mirror's tree and `SessionPrompt` matches what was written.

**Step 1: Write the failing test in `manual_commit_test.go`**

Add the following test function in `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_test.go` directly after `TestShadowStrategy_GetRewindPoints_NoShadowBranch`. The exact import list at the top of the file may need additions (`os`, `filepath`, `id`, `redact`, `checkpoint`, `paths`, `assert`, `require`) — let the compiler guide you.

```go
// TestShadowStrategy_GetRewindPoints_V11ReadsPromptFromMirror verifies that
// under checkpoints_version=1.1, the rewind picker reads checkpoint prompt
// text from the topology mirror ref rather than the v1 branch.
//
// Setup makes the mirror the only ref whose tree carries the checkpoint
// metadata: write to v1, snapshot v1's tip, re-point v1 backward to the
// initial commit, and point the mirror at the snapshot. listCheckpoints
// (topology-aware) still finds the checkpoint via the mirror, so the picker
// proceeds to the metadata tree read we're testing.
func TestShadowStrategy_GetRewindPoints_V11ReadsPromptFromMirror(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)
	testutil.WriteFile(t, dir, "f.txt", "init")
	testutil.GitAdd(t, dir, "f.txt")
	testutil.GitCommit(t, dir, "init")

	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	baseRef, err := repo.Head()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	baseHash := baseRef.Hash()

	cpID := id.MustCheckpointID("a1b2c3d4e5f6")
	const wantPrompt = "only-on-mirror"
	require.NoError(t, checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo).WriteCommitted(t.Context(), checkpoint.WriteCommittedOptions{
		CheckpointID: cpID,
		SessionID:    "session",
		Strategy:     "manual-commit",
		Transcript:   redact.AlreadyRedacted([]byte("transcript\n")),
		Prompts:      []string{wantPrompt},
		AuthorName:   "Test",
		AuthorEmail:  "test@test.com",
	}))

	// Snapshot v1's tip (the commit whose tree carries the checkpoint),
	// then re-point v1 backward to the initial commit so v1's tree has
	// no checkpoint metadata.
	v1Ref := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
	v1Tip, err := repo.Reference(v1Ref, true)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	v1Hash := v1Tip.Hash()
	require.NoError(t, repo.Storer.SetReference(plumbing.NewHashReference(v1Ref, baseHash)))

	// Point the v1.1 mirror at v1's former tip — now the only ref whose
	// tree carries the checkpoint.
	mirrorRef := plumbing.ReferenceName(paths.MetadataRefName)
	require.NoError(t, repo.Storer.SetReference(plumbing.NewHashReference(mirrorRef, v1Hash)))

	// HEAD commit carrying the trailer that drives the picker's log walk.
	testutil.GitCommit(t, dir, "feat\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: "+cpID.String())

	// Enable v1.1 mode.
	t.Chdir(dir)
	settingsDir := filepath.Join(dir, ".entire")
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(settingsDir, 0o755))
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(
		filepath.Join(settingsDir, paths.SettingsFileName),
		[]byte(`{"enabled": true, "strategy_options": {"checkpoints_version": "1.1"}}`),
		0o644,
	))

	strat := NewManualCommitStrategy()
	points, err := strat.GetRewindPoints(t.Context(), 10)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Len(t, points, 1, "picker should produce one rewind point for the HEAD trailer")
	assert.Equal(t, wantPrompt, points[0].SessionPrompt,
		"SessionPrompt must come from the mirror's tree; under the v1-pinned read it would be empty")
}
```

**Step 2: Run the new test and confirm it fails**

```bash
go test -run TestShadowStrategy_GetRewindPoints_V11ReadsPromptFromMirror -count=1 ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy/...
```

If the test fails for any *other* reason (e.g., `require.Len(t, points, 1)` failing because `points` is empty), stop and investigate before continuing — the failure mode must be the assertion, not earlier setup.

metadataTree, _ := GetMetadataRefTree(repo, plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)) //nolint:errcheck // Best-effort for session prompts

## Task 3 Code Review

### Strengths

**Production change is minimal and correctly placed.** The 2-line change in `manual_commit_rewind.go` is the smallest possible expression of the intent: extract the topology ref once into a named local, pass it to the tree reader. The `readRef` name is clear, mirrors the `CommittedRefs.Read` field name directly, and the nolint comment is preserved with its explanation intact.

**`cpkg` alias is the right choice.** The file already has `cpkg "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"` imported and uses it extensively in the lower half of the file. Using the same alias here is consistent, not an introduction of a new dependency.

**No scope creep.** The diff to `manual_commit_rewind.go` contains exactly two lines and nothing else — no incidental reformatting, no unrelated variable renames, no additional changes.

**Checkpoint helpers are established test infrastructure, not a fragile reach.** `CreateBlobFromContent`, `BuildTreeFromEntries`, and `CreateCommit` are all exported from the `checkpoint` package with doc comments explicitly noting their use by the strategy package. They are used in multiple existing strategy test files (`safely_advance_local_ref_test.go`, `content_overlap_test.go`, `manual_commit_test.go` at lines 140 and 310). Using them here continues an established pattern, not a new one.

**`t.Chdir` precludes `t.Parallel()`, and the test correctly omits `t.Parallel()`.** Every other test in `manual_commit_test.go` that calls `t.Chdir` also omits `t.Parallel()`. The new test is consistent with that convention. No risk of interference with parallel tests.

**Test placement is correct.** The new test is added directly after `TestShadowStrategy_GetRewindPoints_NoShadowBranch`, exactly where the plan specified.

**`t.Context()` is used where it matters.** The three calls that produce observable side-effects (`BuildTreeFromEntries`, `CreateCommit`, `strat.GetRewindPoints`) use `t.Context()`. The two `CreateBlobFromContent` calls that don't take a context match the function signature (which takes no context).

---

### Issues

#### Critical

None.

#### Important

**The deviation's path-layout reasoning is stated correctly, but the `summaryJSON` still embeds the session prompt path in a way that doesn't match what `listCheckpoints` actually parses from it.**

The test's `summaryJSON` includes:

```json
{"checkpoint_id":"a1b2c3d4e5f6","sessions":[{"prompt":"/a1/b2c3d4e5f6/prompt.txt"}]}
```

`CheckpointSummary.Sessions` is `[]SessionFilePaths`, and `SessionFilePaths.Prompt` is a path to a file in the tree, not the prompt text itself. The `listCheckpoints` path (in `common.go` around line 1271) reads `SessionCount` from `len(summary.Sessions)` and session IDs from sub-metadata, not from the `Prompt` field. The `ReadSessionPromptFromTree` call in `manual_commit_rewind.go` at line 222 reads the prompt text directly from the tree file at `<shardedPath>/prompt.txt`, not from `SessionFilePaths.Prompt`.

This means the `sessions[{"prompt":"..."}]` entry in the test's JSON is inert: it is parsed and ignored for the purpose of this test. The test still works correctly because `ReadSessionPromptFromTree` reads the tree file directly, and the test places the correct content at `a1/b2c3d4e5f6/prompt.txt`. The test is not broken.

However, the comment at line 509 implies the `"prompt"` field in `summaryJSON` is relevant to the path the picker uses:

```
//   a1/b2c3d4e5f6/metadata.json  — minimal CheckpointSummary, needed by listCheckpoints
```

It says "needed by listCheckpoints" but does not explain which fields of the summary JSON actually matter for `listCheckpoints`. A reader might assume the `sessions[0].prompt` path is load-bearing when it is not. Consider simplifying the `summaryJSON` to only include `checkpoint_id` (the one field `listCheckpoints` definitely reads via `cp.CheckpointID`) and dropping `sessions` entirely, or adding a comment clarifying that the `sessions` array's `prompt` field is not the read path — `ReadSessionPromptFromTree` reads from the tree file directly.

This is important for test correctness understanding, not for test correctness itself.

**`blobErr` reuse across two `require.NoError` calls is mildly non-idiomatic.** Lines 507-511:

```go
promptBlob, blobErr := checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent(repo, []byte(wantPrompt))
require.NoError(t, blobErr)
summaryBlob, blobErr := checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent(repo, []byte(summaryJSON))
require.NoError(t, blobErr)
```

Reusing a named error variable with `:=` (which is valid because `summaryBlob` is new) works but is unusual in this codebase. The conventional Go pattern in new test code written here — including `treeErr` and `commitErr` on lines 525-528 — uses distinct names per call. This is inconsistent within the test itself. Using `err` throughout (as in the rest of the test body) or using distinct names would be more uniform. This is a minor readability point, not a correctness issue, but it is worth noting because the inconsistency is visible in a single 20-line span.

#### Suggestions (not blocking)

**The doc comment accurately describes the deviation but could be shorter.** The comment runs 14 lines, seven of which restate what the code does step by step. The last two sentences of the block comment — "Before the fix the read used v1 (empty tree) → empty SessionPrompt; after the fix it uses the mirror's tree → wantPrompt" — are the key insight. The step-by-step restatement of setup mechanics adds length without proportional clarity. A reader can follow the labeled setup sections. Trimming to the why-this-test-exists and the before/after assertion would keep it at the level of the other tests' comments in this file.

**`wantPrompt = "only-on-mirror"` is a good name.** It encodes the assertion's semantics directly: the value can only appear in the result if the read path reaches the mirror. No change needed here.

---

### Assessment

Task 3 is correct. The production change is the minimum-viable expression of the requirement. The test targets the right failure mode (prompt read uses v1 instead of mirror) and demonstrates the fix. The deviation from the plan's `WriteCommitted`-based setup is sound — the path-mismatch between `WriteCommitted`'s session subdirectory layout and `ReadSessionPromptFromTree`'s sharded-root read path would have caused the test to pass trivially even before the fix, making it useless as a RED step.

The one Important finding (misleading `summaryJSON` comment) is low risk since the test behaviour is correct, but a future maintainer could be misled into thinking the `sessions[].prompt` field drives the picker's prompt read path. Clarifying or simplifying the JSON is a small edit that pays for itself in reduced future confusion.

## Task 3 Code Review

### Strengths

**Production change is minimal and correctly placed.** The 2-line change in `manual_commit_rewind.go` is the smallest possible expression of the intent: extract the topology ref once into a named local, pass it to the tree reader. The `readRef` name is clear, mirrors the `CommittedRefs.Read` field name directly, and the nolint comment is preserved with its explanation intact.

**`cpkg` alias is the right choice.** The file already has `cpkg "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"` imported and uses it extensively in the lower half of the file. Using the same alias here is consistent, not an introduction of a new dependency.

**No scope creep.** The diff to `manual_commit_rewind.go` contains exactly two lines and nothing else — no incidental reformatting, no unrelated variable renames, no additional changes.

**Checkpoint helpers are established test infrastructure, not a fragile reach.** `CreateBlobFromContent`, `BuildTreeFromEntries`, and `CreateCommit` are all exported from the `checkpoint` package with doc comments explicitly noting their use by the strategy package. They are used in multiple existing strategy test files (`safely_advance_local_ref_test.go`, `content_overlap_test.go`, `manual_commit_test.go` at lines 140 and 310). Using them here continues an established pattern, not a new one.

**`t.Chdir` precludes `t.Parallel()`, and the test correctly omits `t.Parallel()`.** Every other test in `manual_commit_test.go` that calls `t.Chdir` also omits `t.Parallel()`. The new test is consistent with that convention. No risk of interference with parallel tests.

**Test placement is correct.** The new test is added directly after `TestShadowStrategy_GetRewindPoints_NoShadowBranch`, exactly where the plan specified.

**`t.Context()` is used where it matters.** The three calls that produce observable side-effects (`BuildTreeFromEntries`, `CreateCommit`, `strat.GetRewindPoints`) use `t.Context()`. The two `CreateBlobFromContent` calls that don't take a context match the function signature (which takes no context).

---

### Issues

#### Critical

None.

#### Important

**The deviation's path-layout reasoning is stated correctly, but the `summaryJSON` still embeds the session prompt path in a way that doesn't match what `listCheckpoints` actually parses from it.**

The test's `summaryJSON` includes:

```json
{"checkpoint_id":"a1b2c3d4e5f6","sessions":[{"prompt":"/a1/b2c3d4e5f6/prompt.txt"}]}
```

`CheckpointSummary.Sessions` is `[]SessionFilePaths`, and `SessionFilePaths.Prompt` is a path to a file in the tree, not the prompt text itself. The `listCheckpoints` path (in `common.go` around line 1271) reads `SessionCount` from `len(summary.Sessions)` and session IDs from sub-metadata, not from the `Prompt` field. The `ReadSessionPromptFromTree` call in `manual_commit_rewind.go` at line 222 reads the prompt text directly from the tree file at `<shardedPath>/prompt.txt`, not from `SessionFilePaths.Prompt`.

This means the `sessions[{"prompt":"..."}]` entry in the test's JSON is inert: it is parsed and ignored for the purpose of this test. The test still works correctly because `ReadSessionPromptFromTree` reads the tree file directly, and the test places the correct content at `a1/b2c3d4e5f6/prompt.txt`. The test is not broken.

However, the comment at line 509 implies the `"prompt"` field in `summaryJSON` is relevant to the path the picker uses:

```
//   a1/b2c3d4e5f6/metadata.json  — minimal CheckpointSummary, needed by listCheckpoints
```

It says "needed by listCheckpoints" but does not explain which fields of the summary JSON actually matter for `listCheckpoints`. A reader might assume the `sessions[0].prompt` path is load-bearing when it is not. Consider simplifying the `summaryJSON` to only include `checkpoint_id` (the one field `listCheckpoints` definitely reads via `cp.CheckpointID`) and dropping `sessions` entirely, or adding a comment clarifying that the `sessions` array's `prompt` field is not the read path — `ReadSessionPromptFromTree` reads from the tree file directly.

This is important for test correctness understanding, not for test correctness itself.

**`blobErr` reuse across two `require.NoError` calls is mildly non-idiomatic.** Lines 507-511:

```go
promptBlob, blobErr := checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent(repo, []byte(wantPrompt))
require.NoError(t, blobErr)
summaryBlob, blobErr := checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent(repo, []byte(summaryJSON))
require.NoError(t, blobErr)
```

Reusing a named error variable with `:=` (which is valid because `summaryBlob` is new) works but is unusual in this codebase. The conventional Go pattern in new test code written here — including `treeErr` and `commitErr` on lines 525-528 — uses distinct names per call. This is inconsistent within the test itself. Using `err` throughout (as in the rest of the test body) or using distinct names would be more uniform. This is a minor readability point, not a correctness issue, but it is worth noting because the inconsistency is visible in a single 20-line span.

#### Suggestions (not blocking)

**The doc comment accurately describes the deviation but could be shorter.** The comment runs 14 lines, seven of which restate what the code does step by step. The last two sentences of the block comment — "Before the fix the read used v1 (empty tree) → empty SessionPrompt; after the fix it uses the mirror's tree → wantPrompt" — are the key insight. The step-by-step restatement of setup mechanics adds length without proportional clarity. A reader can follow the labeled setup sections. Trimming to the why-this-test-exists and the before/after assertion would keep it at the level of the other tests' comments in this file.

**`wantPrompt = "only-on-mirror"` is a good name.** It encodes the assertion's semantics directly: the value can only appear in the result if the read path reaches the mirror. No change needed here.

---

### Assessment

Task 3 is correct. The production change is the minimum-viable expression of the requirement. The test targets the right failure mode (prompt read uses v1 instead of mirror) and demonstrates the fix. The deviation from the plan's `WriteCommitted`-based setup is sound — the path-mismatch between `WriteCommitted`'s session subdirectory layout and `ReadSessionPromptFromTree`'s sharded-root read path would have caused the test to pass trivially even before the fix, making it useless as a RED step.

The one Important finding (misleading `summaryJSON` comment) is low risk since the test behaviour is correct, but a future maintainer could be misled into thinking the `sessions[].prompt` field drives the picker's prompt read path. Clarifying or simplifying the JSON is a small edit that pays for itself in reduced future confusion.

**Relevant files:**
- `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/feat/checkpoints-v1.1-rewind-clean/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go` (lines 163-165)
- `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/feat/checkpoints-v1.1-rewind-clean/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_test.go` (lines 470-564)
- `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/feat/checkpoints-v1.1-rewind-clean/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go` (`CreateBlobFromContent` at line 1818, `CreateCommit` at line 1993)
- `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/feat/checkpoints-v1.1-rewind-clean/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/temporary.go` (`BuildTreeFromEntries` at line 1059)
- `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/feat/checkpoints-v1.1-rewind-clean/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go` (`ReadSessionPromptFromTree` at line 817, `GetMetadataRefTree` at line 770)

Two issues to fix:
1. **Important**: simplify `summaryJSON` — the `"prompt"` field inside `sessions[0]` is inert (the picker reads prompt from the tree file directly, not from the summary JSON field) and the comment misleads about why it's there.
2. **Minor**: `blobErr` is reused inconsistently across two `require.NoError` calls; the rest of the test uses distinct names per call.

```go
// TestListOrphanedSessionStates_V11ReadsViaTopology verifies that under
// checkpoints_version=1.1, orphan detection reads checkpoints from the
// topology mirror ref. The mirror is unadvanced (no ref), so the read
// returns no checkpoints, and a session whose checkpoint lives only on v1
// is flagged orphaned. Under v1-pinned reading the session would not be
// flagged because v1 has the checkpoint.
func TestListOrphanedSessionStates_V11ReadsViaTopology(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)
	testutil.WriteFile(t, dir, "f.txt", "init")
	testutil.GitAdd(t, dir, "f.txt")
	testutil.GitCommit(t, dir, "init")

	t.Chdir(dir)

	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	const sessionID = "test-session-v11-orphan"
	cpID := id.MustCheckpointID("b2c3d4e5f6a1")
	require.NoError(t, checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo).WriteCommitted(t.Context(), checkpoint.WriteCommittedOptions{
		CheckpointID: cpID,
		SessionID:    sessionID,
		Strategy:     "manual-commit",
		Transcript:   redact.AlreadyRedacted([]byte("transcript\n")),
		Prompts:      []string{"prompt"},
		AuthorName:   "Test",
		AuthorEmail:  "test@test.com",
	}))

	// Save a session state outside the grace period so the orphan check
	// considers it. WorktreeID is empty (main worktree).
	state := &SessionState{
		SessionID:  sessionID,
		BaseCommit: "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
		StartedAt:  time.Now().Add(-24 * time.Hour),
		StepCount:  1,
	}
	require.NoError(t, SaveSessionState(t.Context(), state))

	// Enable v1.1 mode. Mirror ref is intentionally left unset.
	settingsDir := filepath.Join(dir, ".entire")

		0o644,

		}

content.text:
I have everything I need. Here is the review.

---

## Strengths

The 1-line swap is exactly as surgical as intended. `ctx` is the first parameter of `ListOrphanedSessionStates(ctx context.Context)`, so it is in scope at the call site with no need for any scaffolding. `NewCommittedReadStore` accepts `(context.Context, *git.Repository)` and passes the context directly to `ResolveCommittedRefs`, which is where the topology-aware read ref selection lives. The substitution is compile-correct, minimal, and touches nothing beyond the targeted line.

The test uses `testutil.InitRepo` with the real git CLI helpers (WriteFile / GitAdd / GitCommit), consistent with the CLAUDE.md guidance to prefer `testutil.InitRepo` over `git.PlainInit` in tests that commit. The test comment block accurately describes the mechanism: checkpoint on v1 exists, mirror ref absent, so topology read finds nothing, session flagged orphaned. The distinction between the write side (`checkpoint.NewGitStore` — deliberate, writes the data onto v1) and the read side (the production path under test, `NewCommittedReadStore`) is clearly implied.

No files beyond `cleanup.go` and `clean_test.go` are touched by this task.

---

## Issues

### Important: `time.Now().Add(-24 * time.Hour)` should derive from `sessionGracePeriod`

The grace period constant is `sessionGracePeriod = 10 * time.Minute` in the same package (`cleanup.go`). The test is in `package strategy` (same package), so it can access the constant directly. The hardcoded `24 * time.Hour` is an order of magnitude larger than needed, which works today, but creates a silent coupling: if `sessionGracePeriod` were ever raised (e.g., to 48 hours for long-running sessions), the test would silently start passing for the wrong reason until someone noticed the constant had changed.

The sibling `TestListOrphanedSessionStates_ShadowBranchMatching` uses `time.Now().Add(-1 * time.Hour)`, which is also hardcoded and has the same issue, but that is a pre-existing problem. The new test has the opportunity to do better.

Recommended fix: replace the magic literal with the package-constant expression that communicates intent.

```go
StartedAt: time.Now().Add(-(sessionGracePeriod + time.Minute)),
```

This makes the "why" — "outside the grace window by a safe margin" — self-documenting and ties test validity to the production constant.

### Minor: `BaseCommit: "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"` — the deliberate choice is undocumented

The zero hash is a valid deliberate choice: the test only needs the session to be outside the grace period and missing from the topology read; it does not care about shadow-branch matching (there is no shadow branch for this session at all, so any commit hash would yield the same result). However, since the sibling tests use real commit hashes and the presence/absence of a matching shadow branch is part of the orphan logic, a reader might wonder whether the zero hash is an oversight.

A one-line comment would remove the doubt entirely:

```go
BaseCommit: "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", // arbitrary; no shadow branch is created
```

### Minor: mixed assertion style between the new test and its siblings

The sibling tests (`RecentSessionNotOrphaned`, `ShadowBranchMatching`) use the standard library `t.Fatalf` / `t.Errorf` pattern throughout. The new test uses `require` / `assert` from testify for setup and assertion. Neither choice is wrong — both testify and stdlib are used elsewhere in the package — but the inconsistency within the same file is worth noting. If a future pass normalises `clean_test.go` to one style, this test will need touching.

The use of `t.Context()` (Go 1.21+) rather than `context.Background()` in the new test is a mild inconsistency with the siblings, though it is strictly better practice. Same note: a future normalisation pass will either update the siblings or revert this to `context.Background()`.

---

## Assessment

Task 4 is correct. The 1-line production swap is surgical and right. The test validates the intended behavior at the right scope. The `sessionGracePeriod` coupling issue is the one thing worth addressing before merging: it is a test-validity concern, not just style.

## Issues

### Important: `time.Now().Add(-24 * time.Hour)` should derive from `sessionGracePeriod`

The grace period constant is `sessionGracePeriod = 10 * time.Minute` in the same package (`cleanup.go`). The test is in `package strategy` (same package), so it can access the constant directly. The hardcoded `24 * time.Hour` is an order of magnitude larger than needed, which works today, but creates a silent coupling: if `sessionGracePeriod` were ever raised (e.g., to 48 hours for long-running sessions), the test would silently start passing for the wrong reason until someone noticed the constant had changed.

The sibling `TestListOrphanedSessionStates_ShadowBranchMatching` uses `time.Now().Add(-1 * time.Hour)`, which is also hardcoded and has the same issue, but that is a pre-existing problem. The new test has the opportunity to do better.

Recommended fix: replace the magic literal with the package-constant expression that communicates intent.

```go
StartedAt: time.Now().Add(-(sessionGracePeriod + time.Minute)),
```

This makes the "why" — "outside the grace window by a safe margin" — self-documenting and ties test validity to the production constant.

The zero hash is a valid deliberate choice: the test only needs the session to be outside the grace period and missing from the topology read; it does not care about shadow-branch matching (there is no shadow branch for this session at all, so any commit hash would yield the same result). However, since the sibling tests use real commit hashes and the presence/absence of a matching shadow branch is part of the orphan logic, a reader might wonder whether the zero hash is an oversight.

A one-line comment would remove the doubt entirely:

```go
BaseCommit: "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", // arbitrary; no shadow branch is created
```

The sibling tests (`RecentSessionNotOrphaned`, `ShadowBranchMatching`) use the standard library `t.Fatalf` / `t.Errorf` pattern throughout. 	dir := t.TempDir()

	testutil.WriteFile(t, dir, "f.txt", "init")
	testutil.GitAdd(t, dir, "f.txt")
	testutil.GitCommit(t, dir, "init")

	require.NoError(t, err)

	baseRef, err := repo.Head()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	baseHash := baseRef.Hash()

	cpID := id.MustCheckpointID("a1b2c3d4e5f6")
	const wantPrompt = "only-on-mirror"

	// Build the checkpoint commit by hand: WriteCommitted lands prompt.txt
	// under <sharded>/0/, but ReadSessionPromptFromTree reads <sharded>/prompt.txt.
	promptBlob, promptErr := checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent(repo, []byte(wantPrompt))
	require.NoError(t, promptErr)
	summaryJSON := `{"checkpoint_id":"` + cpID.String() + `","sessions":[]}`
	summaryBlob, summaryErr := checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent(repo, []byte(summaryJSON))
	require.NoError(t, summaryErr)
	shardedPath := cpID.Path() // "a1/b2c3d4e5f6"
	treeEntries := map[string]object.TreeEntry{
		shardedPath + "/prompt.txt": {
			Name: shardedPath + "/prompt.txt",
			Mode: filemode.Regular,
			Hash: promptBlob,
		},
		shardedPath + "/metadata.json": {
			Name: shardedPath + "/metadata.json",
			Mode: filemode.Regular,
			Hash: summaryBlob,
		},
	}
	treeHash, treeErr := checkpoint.BuildTreeFromEntries(t.Context(), repo, treeEntries)
	require.NoError(t, treeErr)
	commitHash, commitErr := checkpoint.CreateCommit(t.Context(), repo, treeHash, plumbing.ZeroHash, "checkpoint commit", "Test", "test@test.com")
	require.NoError(t, commitErr)

	// Mirror carries the checkpoint; v1 points at the initial commit (no metadata).
	v1Ref := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
	mirrorRef := plumbing.ReferenceName(paths.MetadataRefName)
	require.NoError(t, repo.Storer.SetReference(plumbing.NewHashReference(mirrorRef, commitHash)))
	require.NoError(t, repo.Storer.SetReference(plumbing.NewHashReference(v1Ref, baseHash)))

	// HEAD trailer drives the picker's log walk.
	testutil.WriteFile(t, dir, "g.txt", "feat")
	testutil.GitAdd(t, dir, "g.txt")
	testutil.GitCommit(t, dir, "feat\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: "+cpID.String())

	t.Chdir(dir)
	settingsDir := filepath.Join(dir, ".entire")
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(settingsDir, 0o755))
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(
		filepath.Join(settingsDir, paths.SettingsFileName),
		[]byte(`{"enabled": true, "strategy_options": {"checkpoints_version": "1.1"}}`),
		0o644,
	))

	strat := NewManualCommitStrategy()
	points, err := strat.GetRewindPoints(t.Context(), 10)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Len(t, points, 1)
	assert.Equal(t, wantPrompt, points[0].SessionPrompt, "prompt must come from the mirror, not v1")
}
